en.title: Four Thousand Weeks
en.summary: 人类平均寿命短得令人发指、令人不齿。假设你能活到80岁，那么你的人生仅有四千多周。没人需要被告知时间不够用。我们痴迷于日益增长的待办事项清单、爆满的收件箱、工作与生活的平衡，以及与分心事物永无止境的斗争；我们被铺天盖地的提高效率建议和优化时间的“生活小窍门”淹没。但这些方法往往适得其反。焦虑匆忙感愈发强烈，而生命中最有意义的部分却似乎始终停留在地平线之外。然而，我们很少将日常对时间的焦虑与终极的时间管理难题联系起来：如何最有效地利用我们这四千周的生命。奥利弗·伯克曼借鉴古今哲学家、心理学家和精神导师的见解，为我们带来了一本既具娱乐性又不失深刻的時間管理指南。拒绝现代人徒劳地追求“把所有事都做完”的执念，《四千周》教会读者如何通过接纳生命的有限性来构建有意义的生活，揭示我们许多无益的时间观念并非不可避免的真理，而是个人和社会共同作出的选择——而我们本可以做出不同的选择。
en.summaryOriginal: The average human lifespan is absurdly, insultingly brief. Assuming you live to be eighty, you have just over four thousand weeks. Nobody needs telling there isn’t enough time. We’re obsessed with our lengthening to-do lists, our overfilled inboxes, work-life balance, and the ceaseless battle against distraction; and we’re deluged with advice on becoming more productive and efficient, and “life hacks” to optimize our days. But such techniques often end up making things worse. The sense of anxious hurry grows more intense, and still the most meaningful parts of life seem to lie just beyond the horizon. Still, we rarely make the connection between our daily struggles with time and the ultimate time management problem: the challenge of how best to use our four thousand weeks. Drawing on the insights of both ancient and contemporary philosophers, psychologists, and spiritual teachers, Oliver Burkeman delivers an entertaining, humorous, practical, and ultimately profound guide to time and time management. Rejecting the futile modern fixation on “getting everything done,” Four Thousand Weeks introduces readers to tools for constructing a meaningful life by embracing finitude, showing how many of the unhelpful ways we’ve come to think about time aren’t inescapable, unchanging truths, but choices we’ve made as individuals and as a society—and that we could do things differently.
